comment: Fixtures that a later fixture replaced. Append-only means a fixture file is never edited and never deleted — but it does not mean a fixture can never be wrong about what it pins. A fixture that pinned product data (the version of a shipped pack, the size of its chart of accounts) welded the product to the contract: the pack could not be corrected without the suite going red, which is the opposite of what the contract is for. Such a fixture is retired here instead of edited: the file stays byte-identical and readable, the successor pins the behaviour that was actually meant, and this list says which is which. The runner skips what is listed here. A fixture that is merely inconvenient does not belong on this list — only one whose expectation was never a contract in the first place. SINCE 2026-08-28 THERE IS A SECOND NARROW REASON, and it is written down here because the entries would otherwise contradict this comment: a fixture whose SETUP uses something the data format no longer admits cannot run at all, and a fixture is never edited. That is not a claim about its expectation — the expectation is carried into the successor UNCHANGED, and the guard that keeps this narrow is exactly that. If the successor's expectation differs from its predecessor's by so much as a figure, this is not the mechanism being used: it is a behaviour change, which is a NEW fixture, and the old one stays green or is argued with.

superseded.reason: Pinned `de` at version 2026.2 and its chart at 41 accounts, once via a versioned resolvePack and once via a createTenant that asks for no version at all — so the fixture asserted `the current de pack is 2026.2 and has 41 accounts`. That froze the shipped pack: no account could be added and no version could be published. The successor pins what was meant — the pack resolves, a tenant is built from it, a standard VAT sale posts to the DE numbers — and leaves the product data to the product.
Same weld as de-pack-resolves: `us` frozen at 2026.2 with 35 accounts.
Same weld as de-pack-resolves: `default` frozen at 2026.1 with its account count. Untouched so far only because nothing has needed to change in the neutral pack yet.

Pinned `accountCount: 41` on the shipped `de` pack while testing something else entirely (a full year through the German pack). The same weld as de-pack-resolves, one fixture further on: the chart could not gain an account without this going red. It went red the moment the pack gained the operating-expense accounts an embedding app asked for. The successor drives exactly the same year and pins everything about it except the size of the product's catalogue.
Same weld as de-jahresgang: `accountCount: 41` pinned in passing by a fixture about securities held as current assets.

A rarer case, and the register is the right place to say why it is not an edited expectation. The fixture pins a MECHANISM that still holds: an account a user adds after the fact, which the mapping does not know, is reported in `gapWarnings` instead of being filed silently under its own name. What it rested on was product data — it used account 6050 because the shipped DE chart happened to have nothing there. When the pack gained its operating-expense accounts (6030–6090, so the chart could finally be extended safely) and de-euer moved to ranges, 6050 became a mapped account and the fixture asserted the opposite of what the pack does. The successor pins the same mechanism on 6200, which lies outside every position of every DE mapping by design. The mechanism was never wrong; the example was borrowed from the product.

Pinned `formatVersion: "0.6"` in its expectation, so the DATA FORMAT could not be versioned without this fixture going red — the same weld a shipped pack's version was retired for, one layer down. The contract is that an export states the CURRENT format version, and that is pinned where it belongs: `format-version.test.ts` / `FormatVersionTest` compare the constant against the schema's own `$id`, in both languages. The number itself is the product's. It moved to 0.7 on 2026-08-24, when the partner record gained a `status`. The successor drives the same Z3 export and pins the same streams, hashes and field catalogue.

Pinned `formatVersion: "0.6"` in its expectation, so the DATA FORMAT could not be versioned without this fixture going red — the same weld a shipped pack's version was retired for, one layer down. The contract is that an export states the CURRENT format version, and that is pinned where it belongs: `format-version.test.ts` / `FormatVersionTest` compare the constant against the schema's own `$id`, in both languages. The number itself is the product's. It moved to 0.7 on 2026-08-24, when the partner record gained a `status`. Here it was purely incidental: the fixture is about projection parameters having an effect, and it happened to assert an export manifest on the way past.

Its predecessor was retired for pinning a format version, and the note said the capability lists were 'what it exists to pin'. One capability later that turned out to be the same weld one layer up: the expectation read `summae has exactly these 34 operations and these 22 projections`, so adding a projection made it red — and a library that cannot gain a capability without a fixture generation has the contract pointing the wrong way. The completeness IS a contract and it is guarded where it belongs: `tenant-operations-contract.test.ts` / `TenantOperationsContractTest` hold the published list against the dispatcher's own routing table in BOTH directions, in both languages, so routed-but-unpublished fails as loudly as published-but-unrouted. A hand-copied list in a fixture can only repeat that, at a price per capability. The successor pins everything the description must be right about — invariants with their enforcement, audited events, the journal description, the deliberate boundary — and leaves the length of the catalogue to the product. Retired on the same reading as the pack fixtures: the expectation was never a contract, the mechanism behind it still is.

Pinned `formatVersion: "0.6"` in its expectation, so the DATA FORMAT could not be versioned without this fixture going red — the same weld a shipped pack's version was retired for, one layer down. The contract is that an export states the CURRENT format version, and that is pinned where it belongs: `format-version.test.ts` / `FormatVersionTest` compare the constant against the schema's own `$id`, in both languages. The number itself is the product's. It moved to 0.7 on 2026-08-24, when the partner record gained a `status`. The rest of this fixture keeps being carried forward as the software grows — the capability lists and the audited events are what it exists to pin, and a description that does not mention a capability the software has lies by omission.

Pinned both contentDigest values literally. The digest is derived from the serialisation of the resolved bundle, so ANY field the bundle gains changes it — including a field that is null for this pack, which is what happened when the appropriation plug was added and this fixture, whose own pack declares no such module, went red. That is the same weld a literal formatVersion was retired for, one layer further in: the number belongs to the engine's internal shape, not to the contract. The successor drives exactly the same six steps and pins the mechanism with placeholders — a pinned version resolves to the SAME digest every time, across resolvePack and createTenant alike, while the current version resolves to a different one. That the two versions differ at all is carried by accountCount, which is data rather than a hash.

Pinned the complete `auditTrail.events` list — fifteen object types with their actions — so `systemDescription` could not admit to auditing a sixteenth without the suite going red. That is the census the same fixture's predecessor already retired one level up for the capability list, and the argument is unchanged: the completeness is the contract, the length of the list is the product's. It is also guarded better than a literal can guard it — the audit-trail contract test in both languages runs every state-changing operation and compares what it writes against what the description claims, in both directions, so neither a stale claim nor an unlogged operation survives. `setEntityProfile` (F-CORE-039) is the sixteenth, and the successor pins everything about the trail except how long the list happens to be.

Pinned `tenantConfiguration.accountCombinationRules` as a list of exactly two — the COMPLETE set of combination rules the shipped `de` pack declares — so Germany could not forbid a second thing without this fixture going red. That is the weld de-pack-resolves was retired for (a pack's version and account count) and system-description-invariants after it (the length of a capability list), and this is the same defect written six days after the register said what it was: the completeness IS a contract, how long the list happens to be is the product's. It went red the moment `de` gained `de-kleinunternehmer` (§ 19 UStG: a small business's revenue account may not meet an output-VAT account). The successor drives exactly the same nine steps, pins the same two refusals, the same two correct postings, the same tax-free case that must pass, and the same trial balance — everything except how many rules the German pack happens to declare. That the rules in force are READABLE is a mechanism and moved to a fixture that owns its own pack, `xx-10-constraint-rules-readable`, where the list cannot move underneath the expectation; that fixture also pins what nothing pinned before, that two constraint modules add up rather than replace.

The FIRST retirement for the second reason above, and not for its expectation, which is untouched. Its inline pack declared account 177 "Umsatzsteuer" with `subtype: "vat"` — a value nothing in either engine has ever read. It was inert: the VAT return did not count 177, the cash-basis projection did not treat it as tax, and the fixture passed anyway because it asserts a combination refusal that never consults a subtype. That is precisely the defect the closed repertoire exists to end (format 0.9), so the fixture that carried the defect could not survive it. The successor drives exactly the same seven steps with exactly the same expectations and writes `tax_out`, which is what 177 was all along. Worth recording plainly: the value was copied into a second fixture before anybody noticed, which is the argument for closing a vocabulary rather than reviewing uses of it.

The copy. Same inline chart as xx-8 with the same inert `subtype: "vat"` on 177, same retirement, same unchanged expectations — three `expandTax` steps over an inclusive base, which reads the tax module and never the subtype.
